Xeroderma pigmentosum involves a defect in nucleotide excision repair, which primarily corrects DNA damage caused by ultraviolet light — specifically thymine dimers.  
Deamination of cytosine, depurination, and single-strand breaks are types of DNA damage generally repaired by other pathways (base excision repair, etc.), not primarily affected in XP.  

Final answer: (A)
